chunks.text: Mahsa Rezaei — Founder of Intelligent Nest and MamaNest. Host of Her Career Conference 2026. Session: Welcome and Opening, May 30, 2:00-2:30 PM. Key topics: women in tech, career transition, AI economy, Intelligent Nest ecosystem, future of work. Full bio pending.

Stefania Pecore — AI Expert and Strategy Development Partner. General Director of Women Techmakers Montreal. Session: Closing and Group Photo, May 30, 4:45-5:00 PM. Her career began with the introduction of the first AI and automatic translation subject at an Italian university. She holds a master's and Ph.D. in Computer Science, with expertise in NLP and AI across education and video games. She is an ambassador for Women Techmakers, Women in AI, and Women in Games. Under her leadership, Women Techmakers Montreal grew from 150 to over 400 attendees. She is an AI Expert for UNESCO Women4Ethical AI program and an Ethical AI Expert Without Borders.

Sabah Hussain — 5x Entrepreneur, Executive Board Advisor, Fractional CSO, PhD Candidate in Business Neuroscience. Workshop 1: June 1, online. She integrates consumer and organizational psychology with experience across MedTech, SupplyTech, and EduTech. Currently developing a neuroscience and AI-integrated wearable for young female adults with Down syndrome. Founder of the Federation of Women Empowerment and Support, Women Chamber of Business, and THE CIRCLE. Relevant for women who feel fearful about AI, and those considering self-employment.

Farshad Rouhani — Human-AI Venture Architect, Business Advisor, AI Career Strategy Expert. Workshop 2: June 2, online. He coaches founders and leaders through the shift from AI-assisted work to AI-native organizations. He advises C-suite teams on AI strategy and is known for cutting through the hype to focus on career durability for technologists and non-technologists alike. Relevant for women on the HerTechReady employment track.

Ysimer (Ysi) Gonzalez — Founder of Vantelira Inc., Industrial Engineer, Lean Six Sigma Green Belt. Workshop 3: June 3, online. She spent 18 years managing Fortune 500 supply chains at ABB, Pratt and Whitney, and Bombardier. Now runs a Forward Deployment Operations firm in Montreal. Her philosophy: process before tools, always. Relevant for women with operations backgrounds pivoting to tech, and women building businesses who want to build systems.

Marie-Claire Asseko — Multilingual Strategist, Coach, Digital Transformation Operator. Founder of The Kaizen Gal and Meneva Digital. Workshop 4: June 4, online. Over a decade of experience in SaaS, go-to-market strategy, and business process optimization. Born in Central Africa, based in Montreal. She brings technical depth and cultural fluency to the future-of-work conversation for women and underrepresented communities. Relevant for both tracks, especially immigrant women and underrepresented communities.

Natalie Loop — Founder and CEO of Alygra, a boutique fractional advisory firm helping tech startups build HR, legal, and AI infrastructure to scale. Workshop 5: June 5, online. Over 15 years of experience across startups, scale-ups, and global firms. She operates as a Fractional Chief People Officer for early-stage tech companies in Canada and Europe. Mentors founders through Quebec tech, La Base HEC, Next AI, and Fintech Cadence. Relevant for women considering portfolio careers and self-employment.

Prisca Onyebuchi — Session: BrainDate, May 30, 2:45-3:15 PM. Title and bio pending confirmation. Lin Sok, Dominique Pirolo, Samantha Bateman — Panelists for The Future of Work Wasn't Built for Women, May 30, 3:30-4:15 PM. Titles and bios pending confirmation. Panel focuses on systemic barriers, AI and hiring bias, and career positioning for women.
